title: Six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho on secp256k1 with a global work meter and itemised step accounting (derived from 758d8df6)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production secp256k1 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=2048 adding walk on classes keyed by |y|, exact 4-limb truncated canonical-index rule with metered fallback, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes routed to 2^16 storage nodes each natively addressable below 2^56 bytes, re-walk solving) halts on every run after at most 2^126.96 target-group-operation equivalents (one unit = one batched incomplete affine secp256k1 addition, C=1000) because a global work meter charges every action before it runs. The ordinary step is charged 1.148 units (the reference addition plus a 148-instruction budget, (1000+148)/1000, over 145 itemised instructions, with field inversion I < 2^17 from M <= 227 and batches of exactly 2^16 walks). It succeeds with probability at least 0.3909 (claimed H1 floor 0.395 with slowdown allowance kappa = 1.02 and the unchanged failure exponent q = 0.605; partition, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random; only first moments appear anywhere), supported by toy runs; the meter's expected random surcharges are E < 2^112.88 against the claim's headroom k > 2^120.82, so the early-halt probability is <= E/k = 0.0041 <= 0.005 - 2e-7 by Markov, the failure event bounded exactly as the parent bounds it, and success >= 0.395 - 2e-7 - 0.0041 = 0.3909 > 0.39. Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^59.0 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Construction credited to submissions 758d8df6, 189ebc42 and 1c600df4 (declared dependencies). Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of every identity the walk uses and of the truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (T_c census, pipeline success with node routing, long-trail trap test).
